record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: In axion monodromy and related relaxion constructions, can the backreaction associated with super-Planckian field excursions and towers of light states be kept under theoretical control inside a ultraviolet-complete quantum-gravity model?

evidence.quote: Whether or not these backreaction effects can be controlled in a UV complete theory of quantum gravity is a controversial question meriting further analysis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an effective field theory containing a pseudoscalar (axion-like) field φ whose classical potential is generated by a monodromy mechanism, so that φ admits an effectively unbounded field range while the underlying configuration space is compact. Suppose this effective theory is to be embedded in a consistent ultraviolet-complete theory of quantum gravity (for instance, a string-theoretic compactification or a relaxion-type construction). As φ undergoes a super-Planckian excursion Δφ ≫ M_Pl, two generic effects arise:

(i) backreaction of φ on the moduli, fluxes, and other heavy fields that determine its potential, which can deform or destabilize the potential along the trajectory; and

(ii) the appearance of an infinite tower of states whose masses decrease exponentially with Δφ/M_Pl, in the manner predicted by the Swampland Distance Conjecture, potentially invalidating the effective description.

Question: Does there exist an ultraviolet-complete quantum-gravity model in which both effects (i) and (ii) can be parametrically controlled along a super-Planckian excursion of φ, in the sense that:

(a) the backreaction-induced corrections to the monodromy potential remain small (e.g., subleading to the tree-level potential) over the full traversed range, and

(b) the lightest tower of states remains heavier than the relevant infrared scales (such as the Hubble scale during inflation or the axion mass) throughout the excursion,

so that a controlled effective description of axion monodromy or relaxion dynamics over Δφ ≫ M_Pl is realized? Equivalently, identify obstructions—if any—within quantum gravity that forbid such a controlled embedding.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether axion monodromy backreaction and accompanying towers of light states can be kept under control in a UV-complete quantum-gravity setting remains an actively debated open problem in the swampland program. No consensus model has been established; recent literature continues to debate explicit string constructions versus distance/tower conjecture obstructions.

status_evidence.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews swampland conjectures including the Distance Conjecture and tensions with large-field axion monodromy inflation; controllability in UV completions remains debated.
status_evidence.claim: Controllability of axion monodromy backreaction within quantum gravity is unresolved and tied to swampland conjectures.

status_evidence.title: Lectures on the Swampland Program in String Compactifications
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses obstructions to super-Planckian axion field ranges and the role of towers of light states; presents the question of consistent UV completions of monodromy as open.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of controlled UV-complete monodromy models is an open question.
